problem: The function $g(p)={e}^{-4{p}^{2}}$ models the volume of gas that a vendor can sell, in liters, at a price of $p$ dollars per liter. Find the instantaneous rate at which the volume of gas is changing with respect to the price when $p=1.50$ dollars.
worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate at which the volume of gas that can be sold is changing when $p=1.50$ dollars is equal to ${g}^{′}(1.5).$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $g(p)$ with respect to $p$ is 

$$
{g}^{′}(p)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}p}({e}^{-4{p}^{2}})=-8p{e}^{-4{p}^{2}},
$$

and evaluating at $p=1.5$ gives

$$
{g}^{′}(1.5)=-8(1.5){e}^{-4(1.5)^{2}}=-12{e}^{-9}.
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the volume of gas that can be sold is changing when $p=1.5$ dollars is $-12{e}^{-9}$ liters per dollar.
